# Octree Traversal with LOD & Constant Nodes Also called: Octree Brick Traversal with LOD & Constant Nodes, VoxViz Traversal, main traversal loop ## Overview This method renders a Sparse Voxel Octree (SVO) on the CPU by traversing the hierarchy to project voxels into a color buffer, using depth-sorted traversal and hierarchical culling based on projected size [S1, unofficial]. It distinguishes itself from sibling methods by supporting Level of Detail (LOD) switching between constant-value nodes and textured bricks, and by using a hybrid rendering primitive strategy (points vs. rectangles) based on the projected voxel size relative to screen resolution [S1, unofficial][S2, unofficial]. It builds on [Iterative Octree Traversal](2618-iterative-octree-traversal.md) by adding specific logic for constant node handling and brick texture sampling [S2, unofficial]. ## How it works ### Inputs and Outputs **Inputs:** * `nodes`: A flat vector of `Node` structures representing the SVO. * `eye`: Camera position (`Vec3A`). * `camera`: Camera object providing projection matrix and ray generation. * `fb`: Framebuffer (`ColorBuffer`) with width, height, and pixel data. * `config`: `DrawConfig` parameters controlling rendering thresholds. **Outputs:** * `fb`: Updated color buffer with rendered voxels. ### Data Structures **Node Layout** Each node in the flat `nodes` vector is defined as: > **Unverified code.** The code below did not pass a test run against a reference implementation, or no test fits it, so it may contain errors. ```rust struct Node { occupancy: ChildMask, // u8, bitmask where bit i corresponds to child index i children: [NodeRef; 8], // Array of 8 NodeRef (usize indices into nodes vector) data: Payload, } struct Payload { color: u32, // ABGR format (Alpha 24-31, Red 16-23, Green 8-15, Blue 0-7) } ``` * `is_leaf()`: Returns true if `occupancy == 0`. * `is_occupied(mask)`: Returns true if `(occupancy & mask) != 0`. **Traversal Order** Children are traversed in a specific order defined by `HILBERT_ORDER` for general iteration, and `SORTED_ORDER_INDICES` for depth-sorted rendering. `HILBERT_ORDER`: `[(0, 0x01), (1, 0x02), (3, 0x08), (2, 0x04), (6, 0x40), (7, 0x80), (5, 0x20), (4, 0x10)]`. `SORTED_ORDER_INDICES`: A static array of 48 permutations (8 orders × 6 axis permutations) used to sort children back-to-front or front-to-back based on the eye position relative to the node stem [S1, unofficial]. **Frame Buffer** > **Unverified code.** The code below did not pass a test run against a reference implementation, or no test fits it, so it may contain errors. ```rust struct ColorBuffer { width: usize, height: usize, px: f32, // min(width, height) data: Vec

, // Flat array of pixels } ``` ### Parameters * `min_rect: f32`: Minimum projected Z to draw as a rectangle. * `max_rect: f32`: Maximum projected Z to draw as a rectangle; beyond this, culling is tested. * `max_test: usize`: Maximum pixel area for culling test. * `k_MaxNodesPerPixel`: 12. * `k_BrickStepSizeScalar`: Scalar for brick step size calculation. * `LodScalar`: Scalar for LOD calculation. * `OctTreeDepthMinusOne`: Constant derived from tree depth. ### Algorithm Steps 1. **Initialization**: * Initialize traversal stack with root node. * Set `octTreeNodePtr` to root index. * Set `nodeExtentMin/Max` to volume bounds. * Set `nodeSize = 1.0f`. * Set `voxelHalfSize = RootVoxelHalfSize` [S2, unofficial]. 2. **Traversal Loop (`fast_walk`)**: * Pop `(node_ptr, stem, depth)` from stack. * Calculate `offset = depth_to_offset(depth)`. * Calculate `voxel = stem.extend(offset * 1.73)` [S1, unofficial]. Note: The factor `1.73` approximates $\sqrt{3}$. * Call `on_node(is_leaf, &node.data, voxel)`. 3. **Voxel Processing (`draw_voxel`)**: * **Projection**: * Compute `vertex = center.extend(1.0)`. * Compute `frag = vp * vertex` (where `vp` is the view-projection matrix). * Set `frag.z = -center.w`. * Divide by `frag.w` to get screen-space `Vec3A`. * **LOD Decision**: * Compute `projVoxelSize = ComputeVoxelSize(rayWorldPosition, voxelHalfSize) * LodScalar` [S2, unofficial]. * If `PixelSize > projVoxelSize`, switch LOD (commented-out interpolation logic suggests blending was intended but not implemented) [S2, unofficial]. * **Rendering Logic**: * **If NOT Leaf (Internal Node)**: * If `z > max_rect`: Test rect culling (`test_rect`). If culled, skip. * Else if `z > min_rect`: Draw rect (`draw_rect`). * Else: Draw point (`draw_point`). * **If IS Leaf**: * If `z < min_rect`: Draw point (`draw_point`). * Else: Draw rect (`draw_rect`). * **Constant Node Handling**: * Compute `sampleRatio = pow(k_BrickStepSizeScalar, OctTreeDepthMinusOne - curDepth)`. * Fetch constant value from `data.color`. * Call `TraverseConstant` (implies direct color application) [S2, unofficial]. * **Textured Brick Handling**: * Compute `sampleRatio = pow(k_BrickStepSizeScalar, OctTreeDepthMinusOne - curBrickDepth)`. * Compute `worldRayStep = rayDir * RayStepSize * sampleRatio`. * Call `TraverseBrick` [S2, unofficial]. 4. **Depth Sorting**: * Compute `sorting_order` based on eye position relative to stem. * Determine dominant axis of `eye - stem`. * Return `ChildOrder` (0-47) using bitmask `s` from `eye.cmpge(*stem)` [S1, unofficial]. * Use `SORTED_ORDER_INDICES[order]` to iterate children in correct depth order. 5. **Framebuffer Blending**: * If destination pixel is 0, write new pixel. * Else, extract destination alpha `dst_a`. * If `dst_a < 255`, blend using `a = 256 - dst_a` [S1, unofficial]. ### Pseudocode > **Unverified code.** The code below did not pass a test run against a reference implementation, or no test fits it, so it may contain errors. ```python def fast_walk(svo_nodes, eye, on_node_callback): """ Iterative depth-first traversal of the SVO. svo_nodes: List of Node objects. eye: Vec3A camera position. on_node_callback: Function(is_leaf, payload, voxel) -> bool. """ stack = [(0, Vec3A(0,0,0), 0)] # (node_index, stem, depth) while stack: node_idx, stem, depth = stack.pop() node = svo_nodes[node_idx] # Calculate voxel center/extent offset = depth_to_offset(depth) voxel = stem.extend(offset * 1.73) # 1.73 approx sqrt(3) is_leaf = node.occupancy == 0 # Process current node should_continue = on_node_callback(is_leaf, node.data, voxel) # If not leaf and callback allows, push children if not is_leaf and should_continue: # Determine sorting order based on eye position order = compute_sorting_order(eye, stem) # Get sorted child indices sorted_indices = SORTED_ORDER_INDICES[order] for child_index, mask in sorted_indices: # Check if child is occupied if (node.occupancy & mask) != 0: child_ref = node.children[child_index] child_stem = stem + index_offset(child_index, offset) stack.append((child_ref, child_stem, depth + 1)) def draw_voxel(fb, config, is_leaf, voxel, color, eye, camera): """ Projects voxel and draws to framebuffer. """ # Project voxel center to screen space center = voxel.xyz vertex = center.extend(1.0) frag = camera.vp * vertex frag.z = -center.w frag /= frag.w projected = frag.xyz z = projected.z # LOD and Rendering Decision if not is_leaf: if z > config.max_rect: if test_rect(fb, projected, config.max_test): return # Culled if z > config.min_rect: draw_rect(fb, projected, color) else: draw_point(fb, projected, color) else: if z < config.min_rect: draw_point(fb, projected, color) else: draw_rect(fb, projected, color) def compute_sorting_order(eye, stem): """ Computes child traversal order based on eye position. Returns index into SORTED_ORDER_INDICES (0-47). """ s = eye.cmpge(stem).bitmask() sx = (s & 0b001) sy = ((s & 0b010) >> 1) sz = ((s & 0b100) >> 2) diff = eye - stem a = diff.abs() if a.x > a.y and a.x > a.z: if a.y > a.z: return (sx << 2) | (sy << 1) | sz else: return 8 + ((sx << 2) | (sz << 1) | sy) elif a.y > a.z: if a.x > a.z: return 16 + ((sy << 2) | (sx << 1) | sz) else: return 24 + ((sy << 2) | (sz << 1) | sx) else: if a.x > a.y: return 32 + ((sz << 2) | (sx << 1) | sy) else: return 40 + ((sz << 2) | (sy << 1) | sx) def depth_to_offset(depth): """ Converts depth to spatial offset. Uses bit manipulation to approximate 2^-depth. """ exp = 126 - depth f = exp << 23 return transmute_u32_to_f32(f) def index_offset(index, offset): """ Returns the offset vector for a given child index. """ offsets = [ [-offset, -offset, -offset], # 0 [ offset, -offset, -offset], # 1 [-offset, offset, -offset], # 2 [ offset, offset, -offset], # 3 [-offset, -offset, offset], # 4 [ offset, -offset, offset], # 5 [-offset, offset, offset], # 6 [ offset, offset, offset], # 7 ] return Vec3A(offsets[index]) ``` ### Edge Cases and Pitfalls * **LOD Interpolation**: The condition `PixelSize > projVoxelSize` triggers LOD switching, but the source code shows commented-out interpolation logic (`TraverseBrickInterp`) intended to blend between parent/child bricks. This blending is not implemented, potentially causing visual artifacts at LOD boundaries [S2, unofficial]. * **Precision**: The `depth_to_offset` function uses bit manipulation to approximate powers of two. This may introduce small precision errors for deep trees [S1, unofficial]. * **Culling**: The `test_rect` function reserves space in the framebuffer if the projected area is below `max_test`. If multiple nodes project to the same area, only the first one (in traversal order) will be drawn, potentially occluding valid geometry if traversal order is not strictly depth-sorted [S1, unofficial]. ## Operating characteristics * **Time Complexity**: $O(N)$ where $N$ is the number of visited nodes. Depth sorting adds overhead proportional to the number of internal nodes traversed. * **Memory Complexity**: $O(D)$ for the traversal stack, where $D$ is the maximum depth of the octree. The stack size is bounded (e.g., 256 entries in the reference implementation) [S1, unofficial]. * **Performance**: The method is CPU-based and relies on efficient stack-based traversal and SIMD-friendly pixel format conversions (ABGR packing/unpacking) [S1, unofficial]. * **Strengths**: * Supports LOD switching between constant and textured nodes. * Efficient culling using projected size thresholds. * Depth-sorted traversal ensures correct alpha blending. * **Limitations**: * Lack of LOD interpolation may cause visual artifacts. * CPU-bound, potentially slower than GPU-based ray marching for very large datasets. * Fixed stack size may limit traversal depth (though 256 is sufficient for most practical octrees) [S1, unofficial]. ## Background This method originates from the VoxViz project, a CPU-based rasterizer for Sparse Voxel Octrees [S2, unofficial]. It is implemented in the `svo-cpu` repository, which provides an unofficial reference implementation [S1, unofficial]. The traversal logic is designed to handle both constant-value nodes (for distant or low-detail rendering) and textured bricks (for high-detail rendering), with LOD switching based on projected voxel size [S2, unofficial]. The depth sorting algorithm is based on the work by Iñigo Quilez for volume sorting [S1, unofficial]. ## Sources [S1] marceline-cramer/svo-cpu, https://github.com/marceline-cramer/svo-cpu, fetched 2026-10-27 (unofficial) [S2] apecoraro/VoxVizThesis, https://github.com/apecoraro/VoxVizThesis, fetched 2026-10-27 (unofficial)
